blocks.content: An emergent coast is formed either by an uplift of the land or a fall in sea level, exposing underwater landforms.

rows: Land upliftment or drop in sea level
Land subsidence or rise in sea level
Offshore bars, spits, lagoons, raised beaches

items: Natural harbours are predominantly found along submergent coastlines due to deeper waters and drowned estuaries (e.g., Mumbai Port).
Kerala's backwaters or 'Kayals' (e.g., Vembanad Lake) are classic coastal landform features frequently asked in geography papers.
Examiners often contrast Ria coasts (drowned river valleys) with Fjord coasts (drowned glacial valleys) under submergent landscapes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Emergent coasts result from vertical tectonic uplift of land or a eustatic drop in sea levels.
Submergent coasts occur due to land subsidence or a rise in global sea levels.
Emergent coastlines feature offshore bars, spits, lagunal lakes (Kayals), and raised sea beaches.
Submergent coastlines display drowned river valleys (rias), glacial fjords, and deep estuaries.
The west coast of India (Konkan) is primarily a submergent coast, while the east coast (Coromandel) is mostly an emergent coast.
